llm.summary: The instructions generally match a paid token-scan service, but the skill omits any declaration that it requires wallet signing or secret access (you must sign an on-chain payment), which is an important mismatch the user should understand before use.

dimensions.detail: The skill's name and description claim to call Quick Intel's paid contract-scanning API; the SKILL.md describes the exact endpoint, payment flow (x402), supported chains, and on-chain USDC transfer mechanics. That purpose aligns with the instructions. However, the skill metadata declares no credentials or environment variables even though the runtime flow requires a wallet capable of producing EIP-3009 signatures (i.e., access to a signing key or connected wallet). This is an inconsistency (omitted required credential).
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md tells the agent how to perform balance checks, create and sign an EIP-3009/transferWithAuthorization payment, and retry the request with a PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header. That implies the agent (or the user via a wallet) must produce cryptographic signatures and hold USDC. The instructions do not restrict signing to an explicit user-controlled wallet flow, nor do they warn about never sharing private keys. Because the skill can direct a payment authorization flow, the instructions require sensitive signing operations that are not called out in the metadata.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is instruction-only (no install spec, no files to write, no downloaded executables). That minimizes on-disk risk and is appropriate for a web/HTTP-based API integration.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No environment variables, primary credential, or required config paths are declared, but the flow requires access to a wallet/private key to sign EIP-3009 authorizations and USDC on a supported chain. The lack of declared credential requirements is a proportionality mismatch — the skill effectively needs an ability to sign payments (and real funds), yet metadata does not surface that as a required capability.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and disable-model-invocation is false (normal). The skill does not request persistent agent-level privileges or system-wide configuration changes in the SKILL.md.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill describes a legitimate-looking paid API that charges $0.03 USDC per scan using an HTTP-native payment (x402) that requires an EIP-3009-style signature from your wallet. Before using it: 1) Understand you will need a wallet with USDC (Base recommended) and will be asked to sign a payment authorization — never paste private keys or seed phrases into the agent. 2) Treat any signature as a payment authorization; verify the recipient, amount, and chain in your wallet UI before approving. 3) Confirm the endpoint domain (x402.quickintel.io) independently (e.g., Quick Intel docs) to avoid phishing. 4) Prefer hardware wallets or explicit browser-wallet prompts rather than copying signatures into chat. 5) Expect a real charge ($0.03) per scan — use a small test payment or the idempotency/payment-identifier extension to avoid accidental double charges. 6) Note the metadata omission: the skill does not declare that it needs signing capability or wallet access; consider this a design shortcoming and proceed only if you control the signing flow and are comfortable authorizing payments.
